cases.sentence: Получается так – мы ___ и подлецы, а ты Каин и Манфред…
cases.explain: «мелкие козявки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "As if you don’t know. It works out like this: we’re nothing but gnats and scoundrels and you’re tops."’

cases.explain: «большой нужде» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: "You know what deed. You don’t go to the toilet, that’s what. We felt right away there was something funny. From the time you moved in we’ ve not seen you go to the toilet once. OK, we’re not speaking about number two. But not even number one, not even number one!"’

cases.explain: «грязные животные» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "And why can't you? We can, but you can’t. It works out that you’re better than we are. We're filthy animals and you're a lily."’

cases.explain: «угрюмыми взглядами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: I couldn't get anywhere with them. They had pene- trated to my very soul with their morose expressions. I started to give in.

cases.sentence: Потому что самоограничение, что ли?.. есть такая заповеданность стыда, со времен Ивана Тургенева… и потом – клятва на ___…
cases.explain: «Воробьевых горах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: ‘"No, no." Here I got completely muddled. "In this world there are spheres where it’s impossible to simply get up and go. Because of self-restraint or whatever, the precepts of shame, from the days of Ivan Turgenev and, then, the idealism of Herzen’s youth. And after that to get up and say, ‘Well, boys. .. . It’s insulting. | mean, sup- posing someone had a delicate heart. . ."’

cases.sentence: А когда вернулся, один из них мне сказал: «С такими ___ ты вечно будешь одиноким и несчастным».
cases.explain: «позорными взглядами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: So I got up and went. Not to relieve myself but to make things easier for them. And when I returned, one of them said to me, "With such feelings of shame you’ll always be alone and unhappy."

cases.sentence: Я знаю ___ Бога, но для чего Он вложил в меня столько целомудрия, я до сих пор так и не понял.
cases.explain: «многие замыслы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Yes. He was absolutely right. I know many of God's intentions, but why he invested me with such chaste feelings I've never been able to figure out. And this chastity of mine—this is the funniest thing about it—this chastity of mine has been interpreted so inside out that I have been refused even the most elementary courtesies.

cases.sentence: А потом трезвонят по всей ___: «Он все это делает вслух и говорит, что это не плохо он делает!
cases.explain: «петушинской ветке» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: But, later, they trumpet it all over the Petushki line that "he does it audibly, and he says that he does it not badly! That he does it quite well."

cases.sentence: А лучше я не буду рассказывать все, а только ___, потому что он самый свежий: о том, как неделю тому назад меня сняли с бригадирского поста за «внедрение порочной системы индивидуальных графиков».
cases.explain: «один-единственный случай» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: I could tell you plenty about this subject, but if I start telling everything, I’ll stretch it out as far as Petushki. I'd better give just one single case, because it’s a completely fresh one—how, a week ago, they removed me from my post in the brigade for "introduction of a fallacious system of individualized charts." Our entire Moscow manage- ment quivers with fear whenever they merely remember those charts. And, really, what was so bad about them?
